title: Recent advances in luminescent lanthanide based Single-Molecule Magnets
claim: A genuine synergy in which SMM coercivity below the blocking temperature modifies the emission has not been established, because most luminescent SMMs have low barriers and weak remanence; ligands must still be designed to be both strongly axial and efficient sensitizers, with blocking above about 10 K.
explanation: The conclusions state that spectral changes under an external field are promising for sensors but can occur without SMM behaviour. Except for the pentagonal-bipyramidal phosphine-oxide Dy complex, reported bifunctional systems have relatively weak barriers and blocking temperatures. The authors point to newer Ln SMMs with coercivity up to 60 K as evidence that optimized bifunctional molecules may become accessible.
scope: Luminescent Ln3+ SMMs aimed at magnetic-field-tunable emission.
conditions: Blocking temperature high enough (stated as >10 K) to track temperature-dependent changes, plus sustainable remanence.
caveats: This is an outlook and a stated experimental gap, not a measured cross-effect.
